title: Row Sum of the Unsigned Stirling Numbers of the First Kind Equals n!
description: Open question OQ-03 of bell-numbers-oq-01, the first-kind companion to the Bell / second-kind row sum. The unsigned Stirling number of the first kind c(n, k) = Nat.stirlingFirst n k counts the permutations of an n-element set with exactly k disjoint cycles; conditioning on the cycle count partitions all n! permutations, so Σ_{k=0}^{n} c(n, k) = n!. Pinned Mathlib carries Nat.stirlingFirst with its triangular recurrence c(n+1, k+1) = n·c(n, k+1) + c(n, k) and boundary values, but not the row-sum identity. This entry supplies it by a direct induction on n, and connects the arithmetic identity to the actual count of permutations via Σ_{k=0}^{n} c(n, k) = |Perm (Fin n)|. 3 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide — fully machine-checked.

mathlibDependencies.description: The triangular recurrence c(n+1, k+1) = n·c(n, k+1) + c(n, k) — the sole structural fact driving the induction; splitting the (n+1)-st row sum by it produces n·(shifted row sum) + (row sum).
c(n+1, 0) = 0: the boundary value peeled off by sum_range_succ' when re-indexing the (n+1)-st row.
c(n, k) = 0 for n < k: kills the top term c(n, n+1) when re-expressing the shifted inner sum as the full n-th row sum.
Peels the k = 0 term from a range sum and re-indexes the rest as i ↦ f(i+1); used both to split the (n+1)-st row and to identify the shifted first-kind sum with the n-th row sum.
|Perm α| = (card α)! for a Fintype α; combined with Fintype.card_fin gives |Perm (Fin n)| = n!, connecting the arithmetic row sum to the permutation count.

overview.historicalContext: The unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind c(n, k) = |{σ ∈ S_n : σ has exactly k cycles}| are one of the two fundamental triangles of enumerative combinatorics (the second being the Stirling numbers of the second kind S(n, k), which count set partitions and whose row sums are the Bell numbers). Their defining generating identity is the rising-factorial expansion x(x+1)…(x+n-1) = Σ_k c(n, k) x^k; setting x = 1 collapses the rising factorial to n! and recovers the row-sum identity Σ_k c(n, k) = n!. Combinatorially this is the statement that partitioning the symmetric group S_n by cycle count and summing the parts recovers all of |S_n| = n! — the first-kind companion to the second-kind identity Σ_k S(n, k) = B_n (Bell number) formalised in the parent bell-numbers-oq-01 family. Pinned Mathlib records Nat.stirlingFirst with its triangular recurrence and boundary values but not the row-sum identity; this entry fills that gap.
overview.problemStatement: **OQ-03 of bell-numbers-oq-01 (first-kind row sum).** Prove that the rows of the unsigned Stirling triangle of the first kind sum to the factorial, Σ_{k=0}^{n} Nat.stirlingFirst n k = n!, from Mathlib's triangular recurrence alone, and connect it to the actual count of permutations: Σ_{k=0}^{n} c(n, k) = |Perm (Fin n)|.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Vanishing boundary lemma (mul_stirlingFirst_zero).** n · c(n, 0) = 0: at n = 0 the factor n kills the product; for n ≥ 1, c(n, 0) = 0 by stirlingFirst_succ_zero. This is what lets the k = 0 boundary term dropped by the re-index be reinstated for free.

**Row sum (stirlingFirst_row_sum).** Induction on n. The (n+1)-st row sum is split by sum_range_succ' (peeling k = 0, where c(n+1, 0) = 0) and each c(n+1, i+1) is expanded by the recurrence c(n+1, i+1) = n·c(n, i+1) + c(n, i). Distributing gives n·(Σ_i c(n, i+1)) + (Σ_i c(n, i)); the second sum is the induction hypothesis n!. For the first, a re-index identity hsplit shows (Σ_i c(n, i+1)) + c(n, 0) = n! (the shifted sum plus the dropped boundary term is the full n-th row, using stirlingFirst_eq_zero_of_lt to kill the top term); multiplying by n and using mul_stirlingFirst_zero to erase n·c(n, 0) gives n·(Σ_i c(n, i+1)) = n·n!. Then (n+1)·n! = (n+1)! by Nat.factorial_succ, closed by ring.

**Permutation count (stirlingFirst_row_sum_eq_card_perm).** Rewrite the row sum to n!, then Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin turn n! into |Perm (Fin n)|.

**No decide / native_decide** — the identity is a pure induction on the recurrence, resting only on the foundational axioms.
keyInsights: The whole proof rests on a single Mathlib fact — the triangular recurrence c(n+1, k+1) = n·c(n, k+1) + c(n, k). Splitting the (n+1)-st row sum by it produces exactly n·(shifted row) + (row), and both pieces reduce to n! via the induction hypothesis.

The re-index bookkeeping is the crux: sum_range_succ' drops the k = 0 term c(n, 0) when shifting Σ_k c(n, k+1) back to the full n-th row. That dropped term is harmless because it is later multiplied by n, and n · c(n, 0) = 0 for every n (the vanishing boundary lemma) — so nothing is lost.

c(n, 0) is the one boundary value that behaves differently at n = 0 (where c(0, 0) = 1) versus n ≥ 1 (where c(n, 0) = 0); the factor n in n·c(n, 0) uniformly zeroes it, which is precisely why the recurrence collapses cleanly to (n+1)·n!.

The identity is the first-kind mirror of the Bell / second-kind row sum: partition the symmetric group by cycle count and sum the parts to recover |S_n| = n!, exactly as partitioning by block count and summing recovers the Bell number in the second-kind case.

The final theorem promotes the arithmetic identity to its combinatorial meaning: Σ_k c(n, k) = |Perm (Fin n)| via Fintype.card_perm, making explicit that the c(n, k) are a genuine partition of the n! permutations by cycle count, not just an abstract triangle satisfying a recurrence.
prerequisites: Mathlib Nat.stirlingFirst and its triangular recurrence stirlingFirst_succ_succ, plus the boundary values stirlingFirst_succ_zero and stirlingFirst_eq_zero_of_lt
Finset.sum_range_succ' (peel-and-reindex of a range sum) and Finset.sum_add_distrib / Finset.mul_sum
Fintype.card_perm (|Perm α| = card α !) and Fintype.card_fin

sections.title: Module Header: The First-Kind Companion Identity
sections.summary: Module docstring: c(n, k) = Nat.stirlingFirst n k counts n-permutations with exactly k cycles; conditioning on cycle count partitions all n! permutations, giving Σ_k c(n, k) = n!, the first-kind companion to the Bell / second-kind row sum. Notes that pinned Mathlib carries the triangular recurrence and boundary values but not the row-sum identity. Imports the Stirling development, Fintype.Perm, and Mathlib.Tactic.
sections.mathContext: $\sum_{k=0}^{n} c(n, k) = n!$ — set $x = 1$ in the rising-factorial identity $x(x+1)\cdots(x+n-1) = \sum_k c(n,k) x^k$.

sections.title: The Vanishing Boundary Lemma n·c(n,0) = 0
sections.summary: mul_stirlingFirst_zero: n · Nat.stirlingFirst n 0 = 0. Case split on n: at n = 0 the factor kills it (simp); for n ≥ 1, stirlingFirst_succ_zero gives c(n, 0) = 0. This lets the k = 0 boundary term dropped in the re-index be reinstated at no cost, since it always appears multiplied by n.
sections.mathContext: $c(0,0) = 1$ but $c(n,0) = 0$ for $n \ge 1$; the factor $n$ uniformly zeroes the product, so $n \cdot c(n, 0) = 0$ for every $n$.

sections.title: The Row-Sum Identity Σ c(n,k) = n!
sections.summary: stirlingFirst_row_sum: Σ_{k∈range(n+1)} c(n, k) = n!, by induction on n. Statement and base case (n = 0, closed by simp); the inductive step is the content of the next section.
sections.mathContext: $\sum_{k=0}^{n} c(n, k) = n!$: summing the number of $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ cycles over all $k$ recovers the total $n!$.

sections.title: The Inductive Step: Peel, Re-index, Collapse
sections.summary: The succ case of stirlingFirst_row_sum. The (n+1)-st row is split by sum_range_succ' (k=0 term c(n+1,0)=0) and each c(n+1,i+1) expanded by the recurrence, giving n·(Σ_i c(n,i+1)) + (Σ_i c(n,i)). The second sum is the IH; the first is handled by the re-index identity hsplit plus mul_stirlingFirst_zero, yielding n·n!. Then (n+1)·n! = (n+1)! by ring and Nat.factorial_succ.
sections.mathContext: The recurrence collapse: $\sum_k c(n{+}1, k) = n\left(\sum_k c(n,k)\right) + \sum_k c(n,k) = (n+1)\, n! = (n+1)!$, once the shifted sum is reconciled with the full $n$-th row via the vanishing $k=0$ term.

sections.title: Connecting to the Permutation Count
sections.summary: stirlingFirst_row_sum_eq_card_perm: Σ_{k∈range(n+1)} c(n, k) = Fintype.card (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)). Rewrite the row sum to n!, then Fintype.card_perm and Fintype.card_fin turn n! into |Perm (Fin n)|. This is the combinatorial content: the left side sorts the n! permutations by cycle count, the right counts them all at once.
sections.mathContext: $\sum_{k} c(n, k) = |\mathrm{Perm}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n)| = n!$ — the $c(n,k)$ are a genuine partition of $S_n$ by cycle count.

conclusion.summary: Supplies the first-kind row-sum identity absent from pinned Mathlib: Σ_{k=0}^{n} Nat.stirlingFirst n k = n!, proved by a direct induction on the triangular recurrence, and connects it to the permutation count Σ_k c(n, k) = |Perm (Fin n)|. 3 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide — fully machine-checked.
conclusion.implications: Completes the pair of fundamental Stirling row sums in the gallery: the second-kind rows sum to the Bell numbers, the first-kind rows sum to the factorial. The reusable ingredients — the vanishing boundary lemma n·c(n,0) = 0 and the sum_range_succ' re-index reconciling a shifted first-kind sum with a full row — are the standard toolkit for any identity proved from the first-kind triangular recurrence, and mul_stirlingFirst_zero / stirlingFirst_row_sum are candidates for upstreaming to Mathlib's Stirling development.
openQuestions: The signed first-kind row sum Σ_k (-1)^{n-k} c(n, k) = [n = 1] (an alternating identity from the falling-factorial expansion), and its Lean formalization alongside the unsigned identity proved here.
The mixed orthogonality relations Σ_k s(n, k) S(k, m) = [n = m] between the signed first-kind and second-kind triangles, which would tie this entry to the Bell / second-kind development.

A bijective (rather than inductive) proof exhibiting the cycle-count partition of Perm (Fin n) explicitly, strengthening stirlingFirst_row_sum_eq_card_perm from a cardinality identity to a constructed partition.
